skill.name: AgentDB Performance Optimization
skill.description: Optimize AgentDB vector database performance with quantization, HNSW indexing, caching, and batch operation guidance.
skill.summary: Tune AgentDB for faster vector search, lower memory use, and scalable retrieval workflows.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: The skill is mostly documentation and does not include executable scripts in the package. Three documented npx @latest commands are confirmed external command risks because they fetch and run code from npm. Markdown code fences, local database path examples, and reference links are false positives.

remediation.suggestion: Replace npx agentdb@latest examples with a pinned trusted version and advise users to review commands before running them.

remediation.issue: Commands operate on local AgentDB files
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to run stats and benchmarks against test databases or trusted local files only.

content.value_statement: AgentDB deployments can slow down or use too much memory as vector counts grow. This skill provides quantization, HNSW, caching, and batching guidance to improve speed and reduce memory use.
actual_capabilities: Explains binary, scalar, product, and full-precision quantization tradeoffs.
Shows HNSW settings for search speed, recall, and index build quality.
Describes cache sizing and hit-rate monitoring for AgentDB workloads.
Provides batch insert and batch retrieval patterns for vector operations.
Includes memory pruning, optimization, and benchmark guidance.
limitations: Does not implement AgentDB features itself; it provides guidance and examples.
Benchmark results depend on hardware, dataset size, and AgentDB version.
Some examples use unpinned npx commands that should be version pinned.
Assumes Node.js, AgentDB, and agentic-flow are already available.

use_cases.title: Scale Vector Search
use_cases.description: Tune quantization, HNSW, and cache settings for larger AgentDB vector collections.

use_cases.title: Reduce Edge Memory
use_cases.description: Choose compression settings for mobile or edge deployments with tight memory limits.

use_cases.title: Balance Recall and Speed
use_cases.description: Compare HNSW and quantization settings when retrieval quality must stay high.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Quantization Mode
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a known dataset size.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose an AgentDB quantization mode for my vector count, memory limit, and accuracy target.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Search Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AgentDB workload and suggest HNSW, cache, and quantization settings for faster search.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Memory Growth
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate troubleshooting for a growing database.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze why my AgentDB memory usage is growing and propose pruning, consolidation, and cache changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Scale Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a large production deployment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an AgentDB optimization plan for millions of vectors, including benchmarks, risk checks, and rollout steps.

output_examples.input: Optimize AgentDB for one million document embeddings with limited memory.
output: Use binary or product quantization based on acceptable recall loss.
Increase HNSW connections for recall, then tune search quality for latency.
Add cache monitoring and run benchmarks before production rollout.

output_examples.input: Improve slow AgentDB search for a medium dataset.
output: Check cache hit rate and search latency metrics first.
Use scalar quantization for balanced memory reduction and accuracy.
Tune HNSW search quality after measuring baseline recall.

output_examples.input: Reduce storage use for an edge AgentDB deployment.
output: Prefer binary quantization for the strongest memory reduction.
Use a smaller cache and lower HNSW connection count.
Validate accuracy on representative queries before shipping.

best_practices: Measure baseline latency, recall, and memory before changing settings.
Pin command versions and run benchmarks in a controlled environment.
Validate quantization accuracy with representative production queries.
anti_patterns: Using binary quantization without checking recall loss.
Increasing cache size without measuring cache hit rate.
Running unpinned latest package commands in production automation.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize?
faq.answer: It helps tune AgentDB vector search speed, memory use, caching, batching, and HNSW settings.

faq.question: Does it install AgentDB?
faq.answer: No. It assumes AgentDB or agentic-flow is already installed in the target project.

faq.question: Which quantization mode should I start with?
faq.answer: Start with scalar quantization for balanced accuracy and memory use. Use binary when memory is the main limit.

faq.question: Can benchmark results be guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Results vary by hardware, dataset shape, vector size, and runtime configuration.

faq.question: Is this useful for small datasets?
faq.answer: Yes, but full precision and smaller caches may be enough for datasets under ten thousand vectors.

faq.question: What security care is needed?
faq.answer: Review commands before running them, pin package versions, and avoid exposing local database files.
